label: Confirmed Deaths
contestNote: Toll held flat at 127 for four days (3-6 Sep), jumped to 135 on 7 September (48 direct, 87 indirect), rose to 136 on 10 September (48 direct, 88 indirect), then jumped again to 142 on 15 September (48 direct, 94 indirect) — a 6-person rise in the indirect count in five days — per acting BNPB Data Center head Berton SP Panjaitan. On 17 September BNPB and the Ministry of Health clarified that the 94 indirect deaths mostly involved elderly evacuees dying of pre-existing chronic-disease complications (stroke, diabetes) in shelters rather than trauma or shock — the first substantive explanation offered, though still without published case-by-case documentation. The figure also remains unreconciled with BPBD NTT's own Inatana app count of 120 deaths as of the same 15 September date.

label: Displaced / Sheltering
contestNote: BNPB's own figure moved twice on 8 September (72,864 morning portal figure revised down to 70,382 that evening by acting Data Center head Berton SP Panjaitan), then continued falling — 60,572 (10 Sep), 46,461 (15 Sep) — as verified light/moderate-damage households returned home. None of these figures have been formally reconciled with BPBD NTT's competing 96,385 count from 5 September.

label: Homes Damaged
contestNote: BNPB's Data Center puts total identified damaged housing units at 102,384, unchanged since 7 September. National field verification progress reached 70% by 10 September, but pace varies sharply by regency: BNPB technical expert Jahidin Chilo said Ende district — where the emergency response period closed on 12 September — verified only 1,723 of its 7,030-unit first-phase target (24.51%) in the preceding 10 days, calling the district's pace far behind schedule. This supersedes BPBD NTT's narrower 99,568 provincial tally (4 Sep); figures are described by BNPB as dynamic.
delta: Verification progress: 50.39%→70% (7→10 Sep); Ende lagging at 24.51% of its own target (12 Sep); total unchanged at 102,384

label: Aftershocks Recorded
deltaNote: M0.9–M6.2 range; cumulative count reached 15,722 by 05:00 WIB on 15 September, the 30-day mark since the mainshock (up from 15,156 on 13 September), with ~190 felt by residents. BMKG says M5+ aftershocks (26 events total, 0.2% of the sequence) have ceased entirely over the past week; M4-5 events (476, 3%) are expected to fade in the coming weeks, while sub-M3 events (11,993, 75.9%) may continue for months at instrument-detection level only. Weekly frequency fell from 5,011 events in week 1 to 864 in week 5, confirming the decay-curve forecast.

label: Presidential Visit Status
deltaNote: Twice-postponed visit finally took place on Day 11 (26 Aug); Prabowo distributed Rp200 billion in aid at a Nagekeo Regency command post.

label: Personnel Deployed
delta: 5,832 TNI + 238 Polri + 903 volunteers as of 22-23 Aug (up from 3,500+ TNI/Polri on 17 Aug)

label: State of Emergency
value: Recovery Phase (Province) — Manggarai Timur Extended 3rd Time to 26 Sep
source: NTT Provincial Government / Basarnas / Manggarai Regency
contestNote: NTT's province-wide emergency response status expired on schedule on 12 September, with Basarnas closing its Flores SAR operation and all seven regencies formally entering the rehabilitation-reconstruction (pemulihan) phase. But Manggarai Regency's own Bupati Herybertus Geradus Laju Nabit signed Decree No. 342/2026 on 14 September extending the regency's own emergency status a further 14 days, through 28 September, citing continuing aftershocks and incomplete temporary-housing construction — the second regency (after Ende's flagged verification lag) whose own conditions diverged from the province's declared timeline. Manggarai Timur Regency separately extended its own emergency status a third time — Regent Agas Andreas signed the extension on 20 September, covering 20-26 September — citing continuing aftershocks (including a 21 September M5.3 that collapsed one under-construction huntara unit) and incomplete damage handling; task-force figures put verified housing damage in the regency at 26,185 units (2,458 severe, 4,198 moderate, 7,769 light).
deltaNote: In Ende, BNPB technical expert Jahidin Chilo had earlier flagged the district's 12 September transition as premature given its home-damage verification stood at only 24.51% of target.

label: Temporary Shelters (Huntara) Under Construction
deltaNote: Construction began 17 September in Kampung Bugis (Kota Ndora, Borong); first unit handed over the same day; roughly 2-3 days per unit. Residents may also self-build to BNPB's minimum spec (4x6m) for reimbursement, per Brigjen TNI Mochamad Arief Hidayat, BNPB's Director of Housing Rehabilitation and Reconstruction. A 21 September M5.3 aftershock collapsed one under-construction unit in Satar Kampas (East Manggarai); no casualties, and officials attributed it to incomplete construction rather than substandard materials.

label: Mainshock Magnitude
contestNote: GFZ Potsdam measured Mw 7.61 at 25 km depth vs. USGS/BMKG's M7.7 at 10 km; BMKG's own first report was M7.0 before revising upward.

label: Schools Damaged
contestNote: BPBD NTT's provincial tally rose to 2,633 education units damaged as of 4 September (up from 2,310 on 2 September), still higher than Kemendikdasmen's own 1,918-unit assessment from 31 August (665 schools severely damaged, ~141,207 students affected, only 37 back to in-person classes and 295 on distance learning). A companion Kemendikdasmen breakdown put severely damaged classrooms at 6,927, with 418 laboratories, 1,928 toilets and 370 teacher residences also damaged, and 48,164 school-community members displaced; 785 schools had requested emergency classroom units (2,908 needed), only 89 emergency tents were installed as of 30 August, and 1,221 schools remained halted from in-person learning. Provincial and ministry counts have not yet been reconciled.

label: Aid Distributed (Cumulative)
deltaNote: Up from 2,165 tons (9 Sep); 1,379 tons via Labuan Bajo (West Manggarai) and 664 tons via Maumere (Sikka), with the remainder via other channels.
